gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-saurashtra: Noto Sans Saurashtra is a plain sans whose capitals barely rise above the lowercase around them. Tektur has the louder voice, with tube-smooth strokes and oversized lowercase, while the body font is happy to stay quiet and connected.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-sc: Rounded, ruler-straight and a bit mischievous. Tektur holds a marker-steady line up top, and Noto Sans SC follows with chalky curves that stop short of closing, so the whole thing feels modern without feeling stiff.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Noto Sans Sharada keeps its curves open and its lowercase bulky. Tektur, with terminals that finish exactly as wide as they started, makes a sturdy, easygoing page where paragraphs feel unhurried and nothing tires the eye.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Tektur draws its letters like bent rods of a single weight, with oversized lowercase and openings on every curve. Noto Sans Siddham answers by filling the text line with a large central band and an s whose ends hang loose, so one shows off and the other simply gets on with reading.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Noto Sans Sinhala lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase on every line, with curve endings that keep their distance. And Tektur, stroked without any contrast from stem to terminal, gives that dense texture a bold, distinctive header to push against.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Noto Sans Soyombo has a sizable x-height that suits screens, and its curved letters keep wide, unclosed mouths. Tektur adds a ruler-drawn, constant-width line above, giving the page a crisp, engineered top.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Every stroke in Tektur carries the same gauge, and its lowercase runs outsized with openings on each curve. Noto Sans Sundanese settles into a plain sans rhythm below, its e crossbars open and its capitals barely taller than the lowercase, so paragraphs flow smoothly.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Tektur looks drawn with one pen tip, all pipe-cleaner strokes and outsized lowercase. Noto Sans Sunuwar, a plain sans with curves that leave daylight and short ascender stems, sits below it, handing the page a friendly, approachable text voice.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri packs a tall x-height under short ascenders, with an a whose lower bowl opens up. Tektur is best at making every stroke carry equal visual weight in a loud, distinctive way, while Noto Sans Syloti Nagri does its best work as a plain sans for steady text.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Noto Sans Syriac reads friendly and modern, with tall lowercase bowls like blown glass bulbs and wide, easy s turns. Tektur sits above as a plain contrast, its strokes carrying no pointed-brush swell at all, which gives the two a crisp mechanical edge against the softer text.
